native.capture: Natural Game-view ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshotAsTexture at WaitForEndOfFrame. Real ScreenSpaceOverlay status, FPS and overview canvases stay in their production render mode. No per-camera render target substitution.
checks: Every raster LED pixel unchanged while overlays are visible
Actual queued Tab keyboard input hides all three overlays
First presented hidden frame preserves LEDs during washout
Settled hidden frame has no retained operator pixels
Second Tab restores operator graphics without changing LEDs
Full-display LED allocation omits all operator graphics
native.tolerance: Per-channel byte difference greater than2 counts as a changed pixel; all interior and edge raster pixels whose centers fall inside calibrated LED rectangles are included.
native.command: Unity -projectPath <marked-disposable-copy> -executeMethod OperatorOverlayValidation.Run -logFile <log> (graphics enabled, naturally rendering Game view)
lifecycleChecks: Destroying duplicate FPS/status components preserves the exact real owner reservation and layout revision
Disabling FPS/status immediately hides graphics and releases owner keys; later frames stay unreserved
Calling SetVisible(true) cannot show a disabled status component
Disabling overview hides its independent canvas/cameras and releases its render texture; shared visibility callbacks cannot revive it
Re-enabling each component reacquires layout and restores its canvas; overview cameras/background/render texture return

offline.implementation: Compiles actual production allocator and visibility source with real Unity.CoreModule Rect/Mathf. Screen/Display/controller inputs and clear calls are substituted; actual viewport order and pixel-rectangle methods are copied verbatim. No Unity process, native tracker or device launches.

scope: Synthetic solid-color stimulus and operator UI compositing only. No physical LED receiver, monitor mapping, animal, tracker camera, experiment acquisition or native-player performance measurement. Desktop preview UI Toolkit and replay IMGUI hiding are separate production paths and are not claimed by these framebuffer cases.
